questions.prompt: A new RAM module will not go into the slot, even with firm pressure. What should you do?
choices: Stop, check the notch lines up with the slot key and that it is the right DDR generation
File the notch so it fits
Try a different slot and press harder there
questions.explanation: A module that does not fit is the wrong way round or the wrong type. Forcing it damages the slot or module.

questions.prompt: Put the steps for installing a module in order.
items: Unplug the computer and put on a grounded wrist strap
Line up the notch with the slot key
Press evenly until the clip(s) click closed
Power on and check the memory in Task Manager
questions.explanation: Safety first, then open the clips, align, seat fully and verify.

questions.prompt: You are installing two matching modules on a four-slot board. Which slots should you use?
choices: The two slots nearest the CPU
The slots the manual lists for dual-channel, often A2 and B2
The two slots furthest from the CPU
questions.explanation: The manual defines the dual-channel slots; neighbouring slots often run in single-channel mode.

questions.prompt: Which signs show a module is installed correctly? Select all that apply.
choices: Both retention clips have clicked closed
The module sits level along its length
Some gold contacts are still visible above the slot
Windows shows the expected total memory
questions.explanation: Visible gold contacts mean the module is not fully seated.

questions.prompt: After installing new DDR5 memory, the screen stays black for about a minute on the first start. What is the most likely reason?
choices: The motherboard is training (testing) the new memory
questions.explanation: Memory training can make the first start after a RAM change take a minute or more. Wait before troubleshooting.
